summary: This CSS styles a 'series box' — a callout that lists other posts in a blog series. It uses CSS counters to automatically number the list items, applies a left border and background color to make it stand out, and includes hover effects for links. The code also fixes previous over-styling of the intro text and removes unnecessary dark-mode overrides.

explanations.13: The border-left property creates a thick colored stripe on the left side; var(--mk-rail) is the width and var(--mk-primary) is the color, both defined elsewhere.
explanations.17: The transition property makes background, text color, and border color smoothly animate over 200 milliseconds when they change — this creates a polished feel on hover or theme changes.
explanations.29: The composes keyword (from CSS Modules) imports styles from the global mk-eyebrow class, letting this class inherit those styles without repeating them.
explanations.36: counter-reset initializes a named counter called 'post-counter' to zero, which will track list item numbers throughout this unordered list.
explanations.41: counter-increment bumps up the post-counter by 1 for each list item, so each one gets a unique incrementing number.
explanations.53: content: counter(post-counter) displays the current value of the counter as generated text before each list item, creating the automatic numbering.
explanations.59: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums makes all numbers the same width so they align vertically in a column, preventing the text from jiggling when numbers change width (like 9 to 10).
explanations.64: text-decoration: none removes the default underline from links so they blend with the series box styling until hovered.
explanations.75: This marks the current post in the series with bold text so readers can see which post they're on.
